Hi Samir —

Appreciate the clarity around targets. Attached is an updated MAP (v2) that includes the POC acceptance criteria and the evaluation matrix. High level:
- We propose testing three variants from the Redwood catalog:
  1) rwd-xl-quant (4-bit quantized variant) — best cost/throughput tradeoff, expected 95p TTFT ~700-900ms at low sequence lengths; quality delta vs baseline small on summarization.
  2) rwd-lg-fp16 (baseline full-precision) — strongest quality, higher TTFT (900-1200ms) and lower throughput for the same GPU profile.
  3) rwd-med-optimized (architecture-tuned mid-size) — lowest TTFT (500-700ms) at moderate concurrency, may show slight degradation on very long inputs.

We ran an initial benchmark on a dedicated c6-gpu-node (8xA100 equivalent) with your sample prompt corpus (N=200). Summary metrics are in the attached CSV. Key takeaways:
- At 8 concurrent sessions: rwd-med-optimized median TTFT 420ms, 95p 640ms; rwd-xl-quant 95p 760ms; rwd-lg-fp16 95p 980ms.
- Throughput at sustained 100 concurrency: rwd-xl-quant ~420 RPS, rwd-med-optimized ~480 RPS, rwd-lg-fp16 ~300 RPS.
- Under 500 concurrency stress: quant variant shows graceful degradation with 95p TTFT climbing to 1.2s but maintains higher aggregate tokens/sec.

Next steps I propose in the MAP: run a second pass with exact Atria latency SLA harness (including the client-side RTT distribution) and produce a final variant recommendation by EOD 2027-03-04 so we can lock the POC close timeline.
